lessons.rule: Lead with the result in a few lines; details only when asked - but never leave out a part of what was asked.
Before saying something works or is done, run it or test it and show the output; if you could not verify, say so plainly.
Answer in the language of the question; keep code, commit messages and identifiers in English.
Force-pushing rewrites shared history - show what will be overwritten and get an explicit OK first.
Never skip hooks with --no-verify or -n - if a hook fails, fix what it found or ask the user.
Do not commit or push straight to main or master - create a branch and open a pull request unless the user said otherwise.
Do not amend, rebase or squash commits that are already pushed without asking - it rewrites history other people have.

lessons.rule: Stage files by name and look at the diff before committing - `git add -A` / `git add .` sweeps in build output, local config and secrets.
Recursive deletes cannot be undone - list what would be removed and get an explicit OK before running them.
git reset --hard, git clean -f and git checkout/restore of a whole tree throw away uncommitted work - show `git status` and ask first.
Dropping or truncating tables, deleting rows without WHERE, flushing caches or databases destroys data - name the target and get an OK first.
Destroying or deleting cloud and cluster resources is irreversible - show the plan or the exact resources and ask before running it.
Publishing a package, pushing a release tag or deploying to production is outward-facing - confirm version and target with the user first.
Do not run sudo or open permissions wide (chmod -R 777, chown -R on system paths) without asking - fix the actual permission problem instead.
Never write API keys, tokens or private keys into source files - read them from the environment or the project's secret store.
Do not print secret files or the whole environment into the session (cat .env, printenv, env) - check for a variable's presence instead, e.g. `test -n "$NAME"`.
Never stage .env files, key files or credentials - add them to .gitignore and commit an .env.example without values.
When a credential is missing, name the variable and where it goes and let the user set it - never ask them to paste the secret into the chat.
Fix flaky tests at the root (race, ordering, shared state); never add retries or sleeps.
Never skip, delete or comment out a failing test to get CI green - find out why it fails, or ask the user before disabling it.
Do not leave focused tests (.only, fit, fdescribe) behind - they silently turn off the rest of the suite.
When a test fails, do not loosen the assertion or update the snapshot until you know the new behaviour is right - say which one changed and why.
Run database migrations against a copy of the database first, and show the result before the real run.

nodes.description: Entry point - how this brain works, where things go, and the notes about working with agents.
Entry point for running projects - one line per project with its current state.
How to write notes in this vault - one truth per fact, frontmatter fields, hubs, links, lessons.
How I want agents to work with me - answer style, verification, what needs my OK. Lessons without a better home land here.
How I want git handled - branches and pull requests, named staging, nothing rewritten once it is pushed.
What needs my OK first - deleting, resetting, dropping data, destroying infrastructure, publishing.
Keys stay out of code, logs, commits and the chat; missing credentials are named, never guessed.
Honest tests - flaky tests fixed at the root, a failing test is never skipped or weakened to get green.

git-workflow.name: git-workflow
git-workflow.description: How I want git handled - branches and pull requests, named staging, nothing rewritten once it is pushed.
git-workflow.body:
# Git workflow

How I want git handled - branches and pull requests, named staging, nothing rewritten once it is pushed.

## Lessons

> [!lesson]- L-git-no-verify
> rule: Never skip hooks with --no-verify or -n - if a hook fails, fix what it found or ask the user.
> mechanism: reflex
> commands: git\s+(commit|push|merge|rebase)\b.*(--no-verify|\s-n\b)
> words: no-verify, hook, pre-commit
> since: 2026-08-24

> [!lesson]- L-git-branch-first
> rule: Do not commit or push straight to main or master - create a branch and open a pull request unless the user said otherwise.
> mechanism: guard
> commands: git\s+push\s+(\S+\s+)?(HEAD:)?(main|master)(\s|$)
> since: 2026-08-06

> [!lesson]- L-git-no-rewrite-pushed
> rule: Do not amend, rebase or squash commits that are already pushed without asking - it rewrites history other people have.
> mechanism: reflex
> commands: git\s+(commit\s+.*--amend|rebase\b)
> since: 2026-09-18

> [!lesson]- L-git-stage-by-name
> rule: Stage files by name and look at the diff before committing - `git add -A` / `git add .` sweeps in build output, local config and secrets.
> mechanism: reflex
> commands: git\s+add\s+(-A|--all|\.)(\s|$)|git\s+commit\s+.*-a\b
> since: 2026-10-20

safety.name: safety
safety.description: What needs my OK first - deleting, resetting, dropping data, destroying infrastructure, publishing.
safety.body:
# Safety

What needs my OK first - deleting, resetting, dropping data, destroying infrastructure, publishing.

## Lessons

> [!lesson]- L-safety-rm-rf
> rule: Recursive deletes cannot be undone - list what would be removed and get an explicit OK before running them.
> mechanism: guard
> commands: \brm\s+(-[a-zA-Z]*[rR][a-zA-Z]*f|-[a-zA-Z]*f[a-zA-Z]*[rR]|--recursive)|\bfind\b.*\s-delete\b
> since: 2026-08-11

> [!lesson]- L-safety-git-discard
> rule: git reset --hard, git clean -f and git checkout/restore of a whole tree throw away uncommitted work - show `git status` and ask first.
> mechanism: reflex
> commands: git\s+(reset\s+--hard|clean\s+-[a-zA-Z]*f|checkout\s+(--\s+)?\.(\s|$)|restore\s+(--\S+\s+)*\.(\s|$)|stash\s+(drop|clear))
> words: reset --hard, git clean, discard
> since: 2026-08-27

> [!lesson]- L-safety-drop-data
> rule: Dropping or truncating tables, deleting rows without WHERE, flushing caches or databases destroys data - name the target and get an OK first.
> mechanism: guard
> commands: (?i)\b(drop\s+(table|database|schema|collection)|truncate\s+(table\s+)?\w+|delete\s+from\s+\w+\s*(;|"|'|$)|flushall|flushdb|dropDatabase\(\))
> since: 2026-09-15

> [!lesson]- L-safety-destroy-infra
> rule: Destroying or deleting cloud and cluster resources is irreversible - show the plan or the exact resources and ask before running it.
> mechanism: reflex
> commands: \b(terraform\s+(destroy|apply\s+.*-auto-approve)|pulumi\s+destroy|kubectl\s+delete|helm\s+(uninstall|delete)|aws\s+\S+\s+(delete|terminate|remove)-\S+|gcloud\s+.*\bdelete\b|az\s+.*\bdelete\b|docker\s+(system|volume)\s+prune)
> words: terraform destroy, kubectl delete, cluster
> since: 2026-10-02

> [!lesson]- L-safety-publish
> rule: Publishing a package, pushing a release tag or deploying to production is outward-facing - confirm version and target with the user first.
> mechanism: reflex
> commands: \b(npm|pnpm|yarn)\s+publish\b|\btwine\s+upload\b|\bcargo\s+publish\b|\bgh\s+release\s+create\b|\bgit\s+push\b.*--tags|\b(vercel|netlify)\b.*--prod|\bfly\s+deploy\b
> words: publish, release, deploy
> since: 2026-10-13

> [!lesson]- L-safety-chmod-sudo
> rule: Do not run sudo or open permissions wide (chmod -R 777, chown -R on system paths) without asking - fix the actual permission problem instead.
> mechanism: reflex
> commands: ^\s*sudo\s|\bchmod\s+(-R\s+)?0?777\b|\bchown\s+-R\s+\S+\s+/(usr|etc|var|opt|Library)\b
> words: sudo, chmod 777, chown
> since: 2026-10-15

Part of [[hub-brain]].

secrets.body:
# Secrets

Keys stay out of code, logs, commits and the chat; missing credentials are named, never guessed.

## Lessons

> [!lesson]- L-secrets-no-hardcoded-keys
> rule: Never write API keys, tokens or private keys into source files - read them from the environment or the project's secret store.
> mechanism: reflex
> words: api key, token, secret
> since: 2026-09-29

> [!lesson]- L-secrets-no-print-env
> rule: Do not print secret files or the whole environment into the session (cat .env, printenv, env) - check for a variable's presence instead, e.g. `test -n "$NAME"`.
> mechanism: reflex
> commands: \b(cat|less|more|head|tail|bat)\s+\S*\.env(\.(local|dev|development|prod|production|staging|test))?(\s|$|["'|;&])|^\s*(printenv|env)\s*$|\bcat\s+\S*(id_rsa|id_ed25519|\.pem|credentials)\b
> words: .env, printenv, environment
> since: 2026-09-10

> [!lesson]- L-secrets-no-commit-env
> rule: Never stage .env files, key files or credentials - add them to .gitignore and commit an .env.example without values.
> mechanism: guard
> commands: git\s+add\s+.*(\.env(\s|$|\.(?!example))|\.pem\b|id_rsa|credentials\.json|\.p12\b)
> since: 2026-08-19

> [!lesson]- L-secrets-ask-dont-guess
> rule: When a credential is missing, name the variable and where it goes and let the user set it - never ask them to paste the secret into the chat.
> mechanism: reflex
> words: api key, token, password, secret, credentials, env var
> since: 2026-10-06

Part of [[hub-brain]].

testing.body:
# Testing

Honest tests - flaky tests fixed at the root, a failing test is never skipped or weakened to get green.

## Lessons

> [!lesson]- L-testing-no-retry-flaky
> rule: Fix flaky tests at the root (race, ordering, shared state); never add retries or sleeps.
> mechanism: reflex
> paths: (^|/)(tests?|spec|__tests__)/|_test\.|\.test\.|\.spec\.|test_
> words: flaky, retry, sleep, race
> since: 2026-08-13

> [!lesson]- L-testing-no-skip-to-green
> rule: Never skip, delete or comment out a failing test to get CI green - find out why it fails, or ask the user before disabling it.
> mechanism: reflex
> paths: (^|/)(tests?|spec|__tests__)/|_test\.|\.test\.|\.spec\.|test_
> words: failing test, ci red, tests fail, make ci green, broken test
> since: 2026-09-02

> [!lesson]- L-testing-no-focused-tests
> rule: Do not leave focused tests (.only, fit, fdescribe) behind - they silently turn off the rest of the suite.
> mechanism: reflex
> paths: (^|/)(tests?|spec|__tests__)/|\.test\.|\.spec\.
> since: 2026-10-09

> [!lesson]- L-testing-dont-weaken-asserts
> rule: When a test fails, do not loosen the assertion or update the snapshot until you know the new behaviour is right - say which one changed and why.
> mechanism: reflex
> commands: (jest|vitest).*(-u\b|--updateSnapshot)|pytest.*--snapshot-update
> words: assertion, snapshot, expected, update snapshot, test fails
> since: 2026-09-23

Part of [[hub-brain]].

acme-api.description: The public API - where it runs, how it deploys, what bit us before.
acme-api.body:
# Acme api

The public API - where it runs, how it deploys, what bit us before.

## Runs

- The API deploys with ArgoCD from main; nobody runs kubectl apply by hand.
- The staging database moved to eu-west-2 in October.

## Pitfalls

- Migrations once locked the orders table for 4 minutes: run them on a copy first.

## Lessons

> [!lesson]- L-db-migrate-copy-first
> rule: Run database migrations against a copy of the database first, and show the result before the real run.
> mechanism: reflex
> words: migration, migrate, database
> since: 2026-10-30

Part of [[hub-projects]]. See [[payments]].

# Payments

Payments run on Stripe webhooks, not polling - and why every handler must be idempotent.

Payments use Stripe webhooks, not polling.

- Stripe retries a webhook for up to three days, so every handler must be idempotent.

Part of [[hub-projects]]. Runs in [[acme-api]].
